objective: 0.3.1: assess pi-codex-conversion as a Codex provider for Pi, in particular whether it supports Codex's new context_management system, gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve and comparable Codex features.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "alright for 0.3.1 let's first assess a codex provider for pi", "I'd like to know whether pi-codex-conversion does context_management (the new system), gpt-reserve, auto-review/auto-approve, etc".
This is an assessment only: deliver findings and stop; build nothing until the maintainer says to go ahead.
Testing rules carried from 0.3.0: never run pi or make live model requests; read sources only.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "didn't we agree on using just-bash as the bash tool backend", "we should also support the just-bash's ts/js capabilities (ts as first option, js as fallback)". No earlier record of that choice was found in the original request, the repository, its issues or the Intents.

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-09, after research showed just-bash 3.6.0 is a simulated shell that cannot run host executables): "use just-bash and allow the executables on PATH and other relevant places (cross-platform)". The Pi bash tool runs on just-bash (through Pi 1.5.0 BashOperations); commands it does not implement resolve to real executables on PATH and other relevant locations, on Linux, macOS and Windows, so git, bun, bunx, mise, gh, node and the holyagent CLI keep working; just-bash TypeScript execution is offered first and JavaScript is the fallback.

Codex provider finding: @howaboua/pi-codex-conversion tools.applyPatchOnly keeps Pi read, bash, edit and write plus apply_patch, but turns off its native V2 compaction and Codex prompt while its own Codex provider stays registered (assignment-0mw96dgh6-ud60).

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "about the shadowed commands, prefer them instead of the ones in PATH". Where just-bash implements a command itself (rg, grep, sed, find, tar, diff, awk, jq, ls, xargs and the rest), its built-in runs, and the host executable of the same name is not registered; only commands just-bash lacks pass through to the host.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw the new codex provider should have auto review and context_management". The Codex provider HolyAgent ships has Codex auto-review (tool calls reviewed by the codex-auto-review reviewer) and context_management (Codex server-side compaction) while keeping apply_patch plus the just-bash bash and Pi read, edit and write; pi-codex-conversion applyPatchOnly mode turns native compaction off, so the plan must provide both another way.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "and also, we have the fff integration right? as well as billion context?", "if we don't have billion context and fff the agent I asked to record the stuff in the docs and intents was incredibly terible". Found: Billion Context is shipped (pin 0.1.212, docs/pi/caching-and-subagents.md). fff was dropped by a recorded decision of 2026-10-27 (intent-0mvqtcahb-ipze: "drop fff; bundle ripgrep and fd in the plugin") for the Claude plugin search, and was never carried into the Pi work. just-bash has no record in any Intent, branch or doc.

Default (root judgement, revisitable): the Pi integration adds @ff-labs/pi-fff (0.11.0, MIT, in-process fff Node binding) at an exact pin in override mode, so its tools replace Pi find and grep and Pi prompt guidance stays consistent; the Claude plugin keeps the bundled ripgrep and fd from the 2026-10-27 decision.

Conflict found (assignment-0mw96qjlf-o4zi): Billion Context cancels Pi compaction and rewrites outgoing requests, openai-codex-responses included, so it clashes with Codex context_management (server-side compaction with an encrypted item replayed); its bash guardrails (60 s default timeout, 50 KB output cap) also apply to the just-bash bash tool by name.

Decided (maintainer, verbatim, 2026-11-09): "btw billion context probably conflicts with context management, if they don't work similarly prefer billion, if they do prefer context management". They work differently: Billion Context compresses the history client-side through its proxy and keeps it retrievable (compress, decompress, search_context tools), while Codex context_management replaces the history with an opaque encrypted server-side compaction item that cannot be searched or expanded. So Billion Context is preferred: while it is on (pi.features.contextCompression, the default) the Codex provider sends no context_management, and context_management is used only when Billion Context is off.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-09): "start the spike", "also, billion context's bash safeguards should be turned off if possible". The just-bash spike starts now. Billion Context tool guardrails on the bash tool (default timeout, output cap, repeat detection) are turned off by HolyAgent where Billion Context offers a setting for it; where it does not, the plan says so.

Default (root judgement): the spike runs locally on Linux in a scratch folder outside the repository and is not pushed, because a pushed branch runs the dev pre-release workflow and 0.3.1 has no release branch until 0.3.0 reaches main; Windows and macOS are verified in CI once the 0.3.1 branch exists.
